title: Local bijectivity of a determinant wedge morphism
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C$ a short complex of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $r_2=r_1+r_3$. Suppose $A,C$ are finite locally free of ranks $r_1,r_3$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Let $\varphi:(\bigwedge^{r_1}A)\otimes(\bigwedge^{r_3}C)\to\bigwedge^{r_2}B$ satisfy the following wedge formula, using [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]: on every open $V$, for all tuples a,b,c with $g(c_i)=b_i$, its value on $(\bigwedge a_i)\otimes(\bigwedge b_i)$ is $\bigwedge(f(a_1),\ldots,f(a_{r_1}),c_1,\ldots,c_{r_3})$. Suppose $U\subseteq X$ admits an isomorphism $e:B|_U\simeq A|_U\oplus C|_U$ with $e\circ f|_U=\mathrm{inl}$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ e=g|_U$. Then $\varphi(W)$ is bijective for every open $W\subseteq U$. No exactness away from $U$ and no finite locally free hypothesis on $B$ are assumed.

proof.text: Refine U by opens trivializing A and C and restrict e. Sections of finite direct sums of the structure sheaf are free on the displayed generators over every subopen. The splitting identifies sections of B with the product and identifies f and g with inclusion and projection.

On each chart apply existsUnique_topDirectSum to the bases and transport the inverse along e and the rank equality. Its formula uses lifts from the second summand. The comparison commutes with restriction: standard basis vectors restrict to the standard basis vectors, and on every tensor of basis wedges both composites are the concatenated wedge. Thus it induces an isomorphism of the sheafified exterior powers and their tensor product on this chart.

The wedge formula identifies phi with this local inverse. Apply exteriorTensor_lift_hom_ext on the chart, where g is split epic: agreement on tensors of wedges with second-summand lifts gives equality as sheaf morphisms. This includes sections that only locally have exterior-presheaf or tensor-presheaf representatives.

The refined charts cover every W contained in U. Equal-image sections agree locally by the local isomorphisms and globally by separatedness. A target section has local preimages, agreeing on overlaps by this injectivity; the sheaf property glues them to a preimage. This proves bijectivity on W. Empty wedges cover rank zero, and the sheaf axiom covers the empty open and empty scheme.

lean.statement:
theorem determinant_wedgeMorphism_bijective_of_split {X : Scheme.{v}}
    (S : ShortComplex X.Modules) (r₁ r₂ r₃ : ℕ) (hr : r₂ = r₁ + r₃)
    [S.X₁.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank r₁] [S.X₃.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank r₃]
    (φ : exteriorSheaf S.X₁ r₁ ⊗ exteriorSheaf S.X₃ r₃ ⟶ exteriorSheaf S.X₂ r₂)
    (hφ : ∀ (V : X.Opens) (a : Fin r₁ → S.X₁.val.obj (op V))
      (b : Fin r₃ → S.X₃.val.obj (op V)) (c : Fin r₃ → S.X₂.val.obj (op V)),
      (∀ i, S.g.val.app (op V) (c i) = b i) →
      φ.val.app (op V)
        (tmulSection (exteriorSheafSection S.X₁ r₁ V a)
          (exteriorSheafSection S.X₃ r₃ V b)) =
        exteriorSheafSection S.X₂ r₂ V
          (fun i ↦ Fin.append (fun j ↦ S.f.val.app (op V) (a j)) c (Fin.cast hr i)))
    (U : X.Opens)
    (e : S.X₂.restrict U.ι ≅ S.X₁.restrict U.ι ⊞ S.X₃.restrict U.ι)
    (hf : (restrictFunctor U.ι).map S.f ≫ e.hom = biprod.inl)
    (hg : e.hom ≫ biprod.snd = (restrictFunctor U.ι).map S.g) :
    ∀ W ≤ U, Function.Bijective (φ.app W)
